plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, fragrant mounds send up slender spikes of tiny violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and scent the warm summer air. Whole hillsides and fields turn to rippling purple waves.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to August, with the first flush opening in June
plants.location: Temperate Europe, including the lavender fields of southern France
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: Wide, star-like white blooms float on still ponds and lakes, resting on glossy round pads. Each flower has a golden heart of stamens. It is the largest native wildflower in the British Isles.
plants.location: Lakes and slow waters across the British Isles and temperate Europe
plants.funFact: The flowers open in the morning and close again in the afternoon. After pollination, the stalk coils and pulls the developing seed pod underwater.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is the largest protea. Its dinner-plate-sized flower head is a crown of silky pink bracts around a downy center. It blazes on fynbos slopes in the cool southern winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. Its thick underground stems let it survive the wildfires that regularly sweep the fynbos.
